info_pitch: The installation is a communication platform for urban development, climate issues, ongoing and upcoming research projects at Linköping University. It is intended to be used by the general public and researchers, as well as city officials.
info_how_2: The installation presents a number of different thematic areas that you as a user can learn more about. These are The city and the climate, The city in motion, The development of the city, The composition of the city, and The city with AI. Click on the layers to start exploring the city.
info_data_2: The installation showcases a variety of thematic areas that you, as a user, can learn more about. These include The city and the climate, The city in motion, The city's development, The city's composition, and The city with AI. Click on the layers to begin exploring the city.
info_who_2: The base model was developed using geodata from the Norrköping municipality, with a terrain model produced by airborne laser scanning and manually mapped buildings. The model was then simplified and prepared for 3D printing using the Houdini software.
info_model_2: The section represents what the municipality's urban planning office refers to as the central city. Many of the data layers shown are linked to the strategic work of developing and analyzing the central city. For this work, a strategy has been developed today – a strategy for the central city.
info_software_2: The application's control system is based on the Unreal Engine game engine. The game engine offers the ability to build interfaces that are user-friendly but also reliable in operation. The control system is built with a web-based interface. The application is designed so that the user can interact with the different datasets according to the principle of explore and explain.
info_rights_2: The geodata comes from Norrköping Municipality, Department of Geographic Information, and the map data is produced by Linköping University in collaboration with Norrköping Municipality.
legend_default_bread: Here you can explore Norrköping using projections on the 3D printed city model. Find out how Norrköping would be affected by rising sea levels or where Ostlänken's new railway track should be built.
legend_default_forward: Try it yourself on the big screen on the opposite side.
legend_default_right: Test for yourself on the large screen to the right.
legend_default_left: Try it yourself on the large screen on the left.
rorelse_kollektivtrafik_bread:
The map shows the public transport network. The round circles indicate a distance of 300m from the nearest stop. It is important that as many people as possible have access to public transport in the city.

The municipality strives that the distance to public transport in the central city should not be longer than 300m.

Here, you can see where busses and trams are located in real time. The data in this model is the same data used for traffic information at stops and in apps. The data comes from Trafiklabs open API which communicates with Östgötatrafiken. Can you catch the next bus?
rorelse_trafikbuller_bread:
Here you can see how central Norrköping is affected by traffic noise. The circles around each station show the area in which the noise spreads. All cities with more than 100,000 inhabitants have an obligation to measure and calculate traffic noise at least every five years.

The simulations are made on the basis of many different parameters such as traffic flows, the design of the road, adjacent buildings and speed levels. The noise level is calculated at the facade, i.e. outside the house. How the noise level is perceived inside the house largely depends on how the house is built, how well insulated the house is and what kind of windows there are.

How do you experience traffic noise where you live?
rorelse_trafikmangder_bread:
Here you can see how busy the different streets of Norrköping are. The traffic measurements are done using "tubes", also known as pneumatic road tubes . When a vehicle passes over these flexible tubes, air is forced through the tube and creates a pressure wave that is detected by a sensor. This generates an electrical signal that is recorded by a counter or analysis software. This method is portable and can be powered by batteries, making it suitable for temporary traffic studies.

This is the basis for the traffic calculation model that is then used in the calculation of the noise mapping, which is also shown here in the model.
utveckling_byggnadsar_bread: By looking at the year of construction, we can see how the city has grown over time and where new construction has been added in recent years. Around the turn of the last century, Norrköping was in a boom. The textile industry grew and so did the city. In the middle of the 20th century, the textile crisis hit and production in the central industrial area gradually declined. Despite the decline of industries, investments were made in new housing during the 60s and 70s. Older homes were demolished to make space for new, more modern buildings. After that, the pace of construction has been more limited and increasingly focused on densifying the inner city's various gaps or demolished lots.
utveckling_kulturminnen_bread:
Here you can see which buildings are most valued from a cultural-historical perspective. These buildings have different degrees of protection in order for them to be preserved for future generations. The highest protection a building can have today is to be classified as a building monument, which means that it is protected by the Cultural Heritage Act which imposes special requirements for its preservation. The promenades in Norrköping, consisting of Norra, Östra, and Södra Promenaden, have been classified as architectural monuments since 1994. Within this area, it is not permitted to change the character of the area.

Class 1 is also protected by the Cultural Heritage Act, while Class 2 has a special value without legal protection.
utveckling_stadstyper_bread:
The history of a city always influences the conditions for the city's planning and development. Norrköping's unique history with its strategic location by the Motala river shaped the growing city then and is still shaping our city today. To gain an understanding of what conditions and opportunities exist, one must describe and understand the specific characteristics of different areas based on the historical background.

The city's development can be compared to different annual rings, each annual ring has its own type of architecture and urban character. Perhaps Norrköping's most characteristic urban character is the city grid, which can be found in the central parts of Norrköping.
utveckling_stadsutvecklingsomraden_bread:
Here, areas are marked in which more extensive urban development is ongoing or planned in Norrköping right now. Did you know that there will be around 3000 new homes in the Inner Harbor? Or that the whole of Butängen will be converted into a part of the inner city in connection with the high-speed railway Ostlänken being built?

On the model, you can also see that the Sylten area will get a facelift in the future and that Norrköping's western districts are growing.
sammansattning_15minutersstaden_bread:
In everyday life, we move between several different places and destinations to work, study, drop off, pick up children at preschool, exercise, buy food, shop, etc.

If you have many of these things close at hand, you have a large selection that is available to you. If it is longer to the destination and there are fewer of them, you will often have to travel longer distances to put together your everyday puzzle.

To describe the degree of access to the functions of everyday life, the concept of the 15-minute city has been established — to be able to reach many of the destinations needed in daily life within 15 minutes of movement on foot or on bicycle.

To measure this accessibility, the "everyday life index" (VLX) has been developed. This index quantifies the accessibility of important everyday functions.
sammansattning_arbetsplatstathet_bread: When it comes to the distribution of jobs, it can be seen that it is much more centralized than for residents. There is a large concentration of workplaces within the central city with the highest density within the promenades. The image shows this effect with the help of numbers and statistics.
sammansattning_boendetathet_bread:
Where do the most people live in Norrköping? In this calculation, the city's barriers have been taken into account in order to model how many residents you can reach within 250 meters of each point. The analysis can be used to more accurately calculate data when, for example, planning public transport and school places.

The highest residential densities in the city are found in the Nordantill, Östantill, and Berget districts. After that, there is a relatively high concentration of residents in Haga, Marielund, Söderstaden, and around the center of Hageby. Ljura, Ektorp, and central parts of Vilbergen and Enebymo in turn have a higher residential density than the single-family and townhouse areas in, for example, Skarphagen, Smedby, and Lindö.
klimatet_extremaregn_bread:
A 100-year rain event occurs statistically once every century. The highlighted areas on the model are the areas that are at risk of flooding in the event of extreme rain. In houses with basements, water can also enter via the pipe network. These flood risks are not visible in the model. When the municipality plans for new buildings, flood risks are taken into account and demands are made for various measures.

It could, for example, be about raising the ground level and foundation level when building new houses. But it is at least as important to ensure that large amounts of water have somewhere to go. One of the measures the municipality is working on is to create submerged surfaces in parks and natural areas.
klimatet_havsnivahojning_bread:
The sea is rising globally and will continue to do so for a long time due to global warming. In Norrköping, we still have land rise after the last ice age (post-glacial rebound), but it is slowing down and we will start to see the effect of the rising sea levels. If the global warming is limited, the sea level will rise less.

In Norrköping, we have for a long time not allowed construction on areas that are too close to the sea. For certain developments, there is a requirement that the ground must first be raised before development can be permitted. In the long term, we will need to protect low-lying buildings. Right now, the municipality is investigating the possibility of building dikes along the edge of the sea in certain areas or building some kind of lock in Kvarsebo.
klimatet_trad_bread:
Here you can see where there are trees in the city. Trees in an urban environment are important for our well-being. They contribute to greenery and improve the air which is polluted by cars and factories. The trees in the city also have a equalizing effect on the temperature by using solar energy for their growth. At the same time, the foliage provides shade and coolness in cities on hot summer days. When it comes to rainfall, they can reduce the load on the city's sewage system by absorbing large amounts of water. They benefit biodiversity and provide habitat for birds, insects, and lichens.

The trees are mapped on site out in the field or with the help of analyzes from airborn laserscan data. In the future, AI can help with this work.
ovan_stadskarta1879_bread:
Map of Norrköping's urban area in 1879. Created and published by Norrköping's city building committee.

Through the regulations and extensions of the city plan that came to fruition in 1863, 1873, and 1877, the entire area that lies within the city's planned walking system has now been utilized.

Roughly 27,000 people now live in the city.

Author: Surveyor Alfred Rudolf Lundgren. (1852 – 1929)
ovan_stadskarta1930_bread:
Map of Norrköping's conurbation in 1930. The map was drawn by Norrköping's city engineering office.

With the construction of the Hamnbron, which was opened to traffic in 1915, the appearance of the urban plan changed drastically in that part of the city. Several old neighborhoods such as Lisbon, Paris, the West and East Indies are disappearing. A number of new residential areas have been added, including Oxelbergen, Karlshov, Taborsberg, Pryssgården, Egna hem, and the area between Västra/Södra Promenaderna and Albrektsvägen.

The city's population now amounts to roughly 61,000 inhabitants.

Author: City Engineer John E. Petterson (1878 – 1949).
ovan_flygfoto1959_bread:
This is the an orthophoto covering the entire municipality from 1959 provided by the Swedish Mapping, Cadastral and Land Registration Authority (Landmäteriet) with a resolution of 0.5 meters.

An orthographic photo, or orthophoto, is an aerial or satellite photo that has been corrected to remove distortions from camera angles and the slope of the terrain. This allows the photo to represent an accurate and to-scale image of the ground surface, similar to a map, allowing distances and details to be accurately measured. Orthophotos are used in fields such as cartography, urban planning, and environmental monitoring to provide a detailed and accurate view of an area.
ovan_flygfoto1974_bread:
This is orthophoto by the Swedish Mapping, Cadastral and Land Registration Authority (Lantmäteriet) covering the entire municipality from 1974 (east of Vånga from 1972) with a resolution of 0.5m.

An orthographic photo, or orthophoto, is an aerial or satellite photo that has been corrected to remove distortions from camera angles and the slope of the terrain. This allows the photo to represent an accurate and to-scale image of the ground surface, similar to a map, allowing distances and details to be accurately measured. Orthophotos are used in fields such as cartography, urban planning, and environmental monitoring to provide a detailed and accurate view of an area.
ovan_flygfoto2022_bread:
An orthographic photo, or orthophoto, is an aerial or satellite photo that has been corrected to remove distortions from camera angles and the slope of the terrain. This allows the photo to represent an accurate and to-scale image of the ground surface, similar to a map, allowing distances and details to be accurately measured. Orthophotos are used in fields such as cartography, urban planning, and environmental monitoring to provide a detailed and accurate view of an area.

The process of creating an orthophoto involves processing original images to correct for topographic changes. This image was captured in the summer of 2022 and is a compilation of approximately 10,000 high-resolution aerial images.
ai_asfalt_bread:
The image sequence shows how the AI model gradually learns to identify asphalt and becomes more and more confident in identifying it. It is also possible to see that the AI model is not perfect and in many places errors occur. The fact that these errors occur can, for example, be due to the small the amount of training data that has been in the red training area.

Knowing where there are asphalt surfaces is interesting both to be able to calculate e.g. snow shoveling but also to gain an understanding of hot surfaces can occur. Asphalt absorbs and stores heat for a long time, something that can give rise to a warmer city.
ai_byggnader_bread:
The image sequence shows how the AI model gradually learns to identify buildings and becomes more and more confident in identifying them. It is also possible to see that the AI model is not perfect and in many places errors occur. The fact that these errors occur can, for example, be due to the small the amount of training data that has been in the red training area.

The red areas show the two training areas used to train the AI model. These areas are from a very limited part of the city but can still tell us something about the overall picture of the composition of the whole city.

The training method for the AI model is called supervised learning, i.e. we humans control and help the AI model to understand.
ai_vegetation_bread:
The image sequence shows how the AI model gradually learns to identify vegetation and becomes more and more confident in identifying it. It is also possible to see that the AI model is not perfect and in many places errors occur. The fact that these errors occur can, for example, be due to the small the amount of training data that has been in the red training area.

Is there access to the desired amount of green space in Norrköping? Having access to green space is both a matter of increased experience and quality of life, but also important from a climate adaptation perspective. The green surface helps both to infiltrate water in the event of rain and to reduce high temperatures in the summer. The AI model can measure the amount of green space over an entire city in a way that could not be done before.

trafikverket_etableringsomraden_bread: When Ostlänken and Norrköping's new central station are built, an establishment area for production will be established in southern Butängen. The establishment area includes, among other things, a concrete factory for the production of concrete for the station's bridges, construction cranes and staff sheds, as well as preparatory setup of vehicles/machines and storage of materials. The area is fenced off in its entirety and transport to and from the area takes place through designated entrances and exits.

The streets that are mainly affected are Stockholmsvägen, Ingelstagatan and Ståthögavägen. The main diversion routes for public traffic will be Riksvägen, Stockholmsvägen and Norra Promenaden.

This could, for example, be about changes in routes and timetables for public transport as well as measures that improve the accessibility of the public road network. Some of the measures being discussed are a new bridge for public traffic between Fredriksdalsgatan and Stockholmsvägen and to build the Johannisborg connection before or in connection with the construction of the new station facility.

trafikverket_tillganglighet_title: Accessibility to and from the existing travel center
trafikverket_tillganglighet_bread: The municipality of Norrköping and the Swedish Transport Agency are working together to ensure accessibility to and from the existing travel center as well as important traveler functions during the construction period. Among other things, the possibility of replacing commuter parking lots that need to be demolished when Ostlänken is built is being studied. Replacement areas need to be within reasonable walking distance to the travel center. The distances 400 meters and 800 meters are illustrated in the map. It is estimated to correspond to approx. 5-10 minutes' walk.

kommunen_stadsutveckling_bread: The map shows the future Butängen with a new railway, central station and a fully developed district. The new central station is planned just north of today's station integrated with the elevated railway. Around the new station, an inner-city environment is planned with a mix of housing, offices and commerce, where there will also be space for schools, sports and cultural activities. The new district is planned to accommodate approximately 12,000 apartments and approximately 200,000 - 300,000 square meters of business space.
kommunen_plangranser_bread:
Here you can see the plan boundaries for two of the three detailed plans that are under consultation. Detailed plan for new tracks and station area within Butängen as well as detailed plan for the fourth stage of the Johannisbrog connection with a bridge over the railway tracks.

Remaining parts of the urban development in Butängen lie further in the future and will be planned in stages.

Parts of the Loddby railway plan can also be seen here.

kommunen_trafik_bread:
The elevated railway creates opportunities - partly to seamlessly link the parts of the inner city and traffic routes, partly to locate many of the station's surface-requiring functions under the bridge, which provides good conditions for short switching times and urban development.

Drottninggatan is extended as the natural main axis of the city centre, with a new station building under the bridge that will have access to the trains on both sides of the street. Bicycle parking, public transport stop locations, taxi zone, etc. placed close to each other and station building. Places are also placed under the bridge for easy pick-up and drop-off by car, as well as a parking garage.

The central parts around the station form a coherent zone where walking, cycling and public transport are prioritized.
kommunen_torg_bread:
The first detailed plan includes some of the most important parks and square formations in the future Butängen.

The strip of places and parks along Drottninggatan is extended through the station area, from Carl Johans park, past Norra Promenaden and into Butängen. The existing station building and new station square form a southern entrance to the new station, the line then continues under the elevated railway and a new park with a larger playground is planned at the station's northern entrance. Parkways are planned along Fredriksdalsgatan and the railway bridge with open stormwater solutions that will be led further in a channel towards Bråviken. Streets get trees or other greenery that contributes to a good microclimate and the integration of green structure in the city.
